Ekal and Vakni crept silently into the Saen's forests, careful to avoid alerting any of the Thorac or Saen who wandered therein. They sought the forest of primroses, and the plants that grew among the trees there. Their master, Valdi, god of thieves and deception, had told them to steal from the trees among that forest only a few small pouches of the primrose berries that grew there, and he warned them not to touch the plant directly, or they would certainly die. Why they should journey this far into the land of the Saen he did not say. Ekal was sure such a small amount of the vine would not have been missed from the areas nearer to the Thorac villages, where the Saen grew small patches (to deter threats, such as Ekal and Vakni, she surmised). Perhaps these were more potent? Though it was not her place to question her god, so she traveled onward as the uncertainty gnawed at her mind.

Lost in thought as she was, the primrose forest came on nearly unexpected, and, had Vakni not halted her in that moment, Ekal may have run straight into a vine that hung low above her head. They signaled each other and entered the woods, placing each step deliberately. The vines were more dense here, this was true. Perhaps this is why they had been made to travel to the source of the vine. They journeyed inward to the forest, unable to find any blossoms on the outer edge of the wood. Ekal caught a glimpse of purple to her right and ventured carefully towards the blossom. She had been certain she had seen it. There! Another glimpse of the blossom, but where had it gone? As she glanced around, she realized that Vakni was nowhere to be seen. She dared not call out to him, lest she jeopardize their mission, but she traveled quickly to find him.

She followed back where she had come, she thought, but could find no trace of her companion. She searched desperately for his trail, but it was as if he had never been there. Even her own tracks seems to disappear when she was not looking. Had she touched the vine?! Was her mind truly lost?! She caught sight of a road through the trees and slowly crept towards the yellow paving stones. She did not remember this road, but perhaps it would lead her to Vakni. She hesitated. Vakni...Valdi...her god would be furious if she let herself become so foolishly lost on such a simple mission. Had he heard her doubts? Perhaps this was her punishment!

She did not even notice as the serpent crept beneath her feet. It had grown fat on the berries and vines of the Primrose Path, let alone the consumption of it's own flesh, and now, as it slithered across the ground, it appeared itself to be a writhing path. She stared down at the yellow path from a distance, waiting for a sign of motion, and the serpent was upon her.

Ouroboros wrapped its writhing mass of writhing flesh around her form, its body moist with the secretions of a diet consisting of nothing more than primrose of its own roiling flesh. Ekal's mind raced. Her training left her. She couldn't move. She couldn't speak. Was this the end? Would she die here? Was this a test? Where was Vakni? She stabbed at the beast with her blade, no longer sure of what to do, she simply lashed out at every writhing inch she could find. Her blows fell even on her own body, until suddenly her arm was pinned as well, and she could see the wriggling mass as it brought her into itself.

She woke suddenly, sputtering and coughing as a warm liquid ran down her throat. She reached for her blade, but it was gone. Her mind was clear now, and she knew she must defend herself against the beast.

The beast? Where had it gone? She was on the road she had seen from the forest. How had she gotten here? And who was this man with the goblet of warm liquid that smiled down at her so condescendingly? She would have his heart for that...

"Relax you silly creature. You walked among my trees and expected to walk away without saying hello? Dear me. I told Valdi to send me the servant of surest conviction, but you, my dear, seem unaware of the bargain. Perhaps that is for the best. I am Cruxius, god of Uncertainty, Hesitation, and Crossroads, such as the one you now find yourself upon. I do apologize for Ouroboros. I had asked him to fetch you from the woods, but I do wish he had been more gentle with you. He sometimes forgets how large he has grown, especially when he travels to the primrose forests that serve as a connection to my realm from your world, and judging by the poison you are now covered in, I should have commanded him not to touch you as well. Ah, such is life. Oh dear, do not look so panicked. The poison is perfectly harmless to you now. My goblet, which you so rudely coughed into, is filled with the drink of my followers, aqua animi, which is also the cure for the primrose's poison."

Ekal attempted to scrape some of the viscous *mucus* from her body. This man was truly a god? What is an Ouroboros? Where was Valdi? And Vakni? She was bleeding from wounds where she had stabbed herself in the struggle. Foolish!

"Here, allow me." Cruxius waved his hand, and Ekal stood as she had, but free of the poison that had engulfed her, wounds healed as if by magic. "Now focus, Ekal." He knew her name?! "Yes Ekal, I know who you are. Your god, my brother Valdi, has asked for my assistance, and though I publicly denied his request, I offered him a deal, in secret. God of deception that he is, he agreed to my terms. The first of those terms was a favour owed, but the last, my dear, was you."

Ekal's mind raced. Her? She was a bargaining chip? Had she been deceived by her own god? What had she done to anger him so? Had he, too, heard her doubts? What a fool she had been!

"You, dear child, will be the first to follow me. I do not ask that you revoke your brother or your tasks, but only that you worship me. Should your conviction to me be as strong as Valdi claims, I will teach you the making of aqua animi, and you may use it yet to aid your brother. Right now he searches for you among the trees. I can see him as Ouroboros sees him, for he is the avatar of my will. The same beast that brought you to me has poisoned your brother so that you may be certain of my words."

Poisoned Vakni?! How could that be? But if she could not stop the beast before...

"I have brought you a [gift](http://i.imgur.com/DVdZtIO.jpg), my dear. Inside this there are enough doses of aqua animi to cure your brother and about two dozen of the Thorac. Valdi still has a mission for you, and it is my will that his mission be done. I will send the Thorac doubt and uncertainty of their own flesh as they have never known, at Valdi's request, with the berries you will gather before returning to him. Dry the berries in the sun until their flesh is dry and cracked. Grind them into a fine powder, and mix the powder with a few drops of water. This clear paste you will spread among the Thorac tribes. Place it on fruits, that they may consume it, on clothing, that they might wear it, and in water, that they might drink it. When uncertainty rules the minds of the Thorac, then will you and your brother come forth as saviors, providing the antidote for those you can still save. If they should ask you why, you will tell them because you are grateful for their bounties, which they have shared, and because Valdi, whom you will call your god, has taken pity on them. You will tell them that you came to ask if any would like to learn the ways of stealth, so that they might better hunt game, which Valdi has taught to you, and has commanded you to do. Seeing the Thorac so broken, you will ask if, instead, any of them would join you, for surely someone in the forest has forsaken them to cause such strife among the villages, and that you will beg Valdi to take them in, should they wish to come. I will sow the seeds of doubt in their minds, such that some will believe the Saen responsible for the death of their brothers and sisters, and they will follow you. Return to me then, in the forest where your brother now lies, if my words prove true, and bring with you any Thorac worthy of the secrets, for I will teach then my followers the making of aqua animi, that they may never fear the fruit of my tree. Go now. Save your brother that you may know my words to be true. Turn to the woods and run. Follow the writhing mass that is Ouroboros, and you will find your brother."

Ekal did not hesitate. She clasped onto her arm the flask of aqua animi and ran into the woods. She found Ouroboros quickly, though still not sure what the beast was, and followed the grey, writhing mass. After a few moments, she came upon her brother, Vakni, lying on the ground, with his arm stuck inside Ouroboros' flesh. He had fought. She could see many marks upon the beast, though they appeared to be healing rapidly, and even upon Vakni himself, as if he, too, had landed uncertain blows upon his own form. His breathing was ragged, his eyes wild, as if he still did battle with a demon in his own mind. As she approached, Ouroboros released Vakni, and disappeared back into the woods. She poured some of the liquid from the flask on her wrist down his throat, and prayed that the Cruxius would prove true to his word. Sure enough, Vakni soon regained his senses and vowed never to speak of the conflict. He asked Ekal what had happened, and she told him the story of the man on the gilded road...

It will have multiple electric motors (for propulsion) in the Catamarans) as well as hydro-electric turbines in both catamarans. The top deck's roof will be a giant solar array and there will be Wind Turbines on all 4 corners of the roof as well. All lighting will be achieved via Low-Voltage High-Output LED lights integrated into the hull, walls, ceilings, cabinets, etc. There will be a small Greenhouse on the upper deck with Water-Driven rotating grow bins where we grow our own Vegetables, Herbs and some Fruits. There will be an on-board Desalinization System capable of converting sea water to Potable Water (for us or the Greenhouse) at a rate of 10-20 Gallons per minute.
